--- original

@@ -0,0 +1,21 @@
+---
+position_column: todo
+position_ordinal: '9980'
+title: 'Multi-consumer onReload: commandUpdates must not steal reload ticks'
+---
+## What
+Variance from §7.1 (one registry, four simultaneous consumers) and §6 ("commandUpdates ticks on every reload"): `onReload` is a single `AsyncStream` with one continuation (`Registry/SkillsRegistry.swift:154, 274-284, 836-840`), and `commandUpdates` CONSUMES that same stream (`Registry/SkillsRegistry+SlashCommands.swift:49-59`). Two `for await` consumers split elements — a host that forwards metadata to the searcher AND reads `commandUpdates` loses an arbitrary share of ticks on each side; each fresh `commandUpdates` access adds another competing consumer.
+
+Fix: multicast reload events — e.g. keep a locked array of continuations, each `onReload`/`commandUpdates` access registers its own stream, every rebuild publishes to all registered continuations (and finishes them on deinit). Update the single-subscriber doc comment (`+SlashCommands.swift:44-48`).
+
+## Acceptance Criteria
+- [ ] Two concurrent consumers (one `onReload`, one `commandUpdates`) BOTH observe every reload in a 5-reload burst
+- [ ] A second, late `commandUpdates` subscriber receives subsequent ticks
+- [ ] Streams finish cleanly on registry deinit (no leaked continuations)
+
+## Tests
+- [ ] Extend `Tests/FoundationModelsSkillsTests/SkillsRegistryReloadTests.swift` — dual-consumer burst case; late-subscriber case; deinit-finish case
+- [ ] `swift test` — exit 0
+
+## Workflow
+- Use `/tdd` — write failing tests first, then implement to make them pass.
\ No newline at end of file

@@ -1,4 +1,16 @@
 ---
+comments:
+- actor: claude-code
+  id: 01kyr3v5c0xnbnycr1qaa1ated
+  text: |-
+    Implemented and checkpointed at 055577e:
+    - `SkillsRegistry.onReload` is now computed, not a stored `let`: each access registers an independent subscriber against a new `ReloadBroadcaster` (a locked dictionary of continuations owned by `ReloadCoordinator`), instead of returning the one shared `AsyncStream` every prior consumer competed over. `publish(_:)` yields to every registered continuation on each rebuild; `finishAll()` (called from `ReloadCoordinator.deinit`) finishes every one, not just one.
+    - `commandUpdates` needed no behavioral change (it already re-subscribes to `onReload` per access) but its doc comment was stale ("mirrors onReload's own single-subscriber contract") — updated.
+    - Along the way, found and fixed a real latent retain-cycle bug `commandUpdates`'s own bridging `Task` had: it captured `self` (a whole `SkillsRegistry` struct copy, since it called `self.slashCommands()`) — since `SkillsRegistry` is a value type, that copy carried its own strong reference to `reloadCoordinator`, keeping the watcher alive for the task's lifetime regardless of the owning registry's actual lifetime. Fixed via a new `internal var detachedReader: SkillsRegistry` (reload-disabled view sharing the live `catalogBox`) that the bridging task captures instead. Caught by my own new deinit test — it hung the first run.
+    - New tests in `SkillsRegistryReloadTests.swift`: two concurrent consumers (`onReload` + `commandUpdates`) both observe all 5 reloads in a burst; a late `commandUpdates` subscriber (registered after the first reload already happened) still observes every subsequent tick; every subscriber (both `onReload` and `commandUpdates`) finishes cleanly on registry deinit.
+    - Full suite green: 277/277 tests passing.
+    - Scoped review running in background (task ktyx9ydyk) — awaiting result.
+  timestamp: 2026-07-29T23:37:33.824586+00:00
